title: Raised beds and bunk-bed design review
intro: Elevated and bunk beds need specialist verification of falls, entrapment, support and access. Prepare a traceable review record; the figures are hazard maps, not construction drawings.
goals: Identify the product, user and market
Review guards, mattress and openings as a system

sections.title: Identify the product, user and market
sections.text: Identify the product definition, intended user and market. US reference 16 CFR 1513 addresses elevated children’s beds within its scope and requires the warning against upper-bunk use below age 6. Reaching 6 does not itself establish suitability. Verify current requirements for the intended market and product; the absence of a lower bed does not automatically exclude a loft bed from review.
sections.caption: Classify first; a US reference does not replace local applicability review.

sections.title: Review guards, mattress and openings as a system
sections.text: Mark guards relative to the specified mattress, end openings, wall interfaces, ladder route and supports. A thicker mattress changes the exposed guard height; do not improvise an added rail. Entrapment assessment depends on opening shape, location and defined test methods, not one general gap rule. Never use a child’s head or body as a test probe.
sections.caption: Review the mattress, guards and openings together; a sketch is not a test result.

sections.title: Require traceable verification evidence
sections.text: Link applicable requirement, drawing revision, product/mattress identity, verifier, result and outstanding action. CPSC guidance explains accepted third-party testing, children’s product certification and additional US requirements; establish what applies in the project’s market. Obtain assembly, labeling and service instructions. A visual prototype or one adult standing on a bed is not a substitute for required system testing.
sections.caption: Requirement + identified configuration + traceable result.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: The exercise proposes an upper bunk for a 4-year-old and provides only an unidentified image. Reject that allocation and review an appropriate non-elevated sleeping alternative with product verification. Even changing the user’s age would not resolve the separate absence of system evidence.
example.decision: Decision: reject the upper-bunk allocation and obtain evidence for a suitable alternative.

quiz.question: Do an image and one informal load trial establish safety?
options: No; traceable system verification is needed
Yes, if the child is older than 6
quiz.explanation: Classification, guards, mattress, openings, supports and applicable tests concern the identified system.

assignment.prompt: Prepare an elevated-bed review register covering classification, hazards, applicable requirements, missing evidence and disposition, without a construction detail.

faq.question: Is a loft bed without a lower bunk automatically excluded?
faq.answer: No. Check the applicable product definition and scope rather than relying on its marketing name.
